core.title: Keep commons at theme index 0 in the repository theme map
core.given: A repository's theme map (the plan artifact that declares the repository's resolved theme set) is authoritative and repository-owned; its only package-supplied entry is commons at index 0.
core.when: The theme map is created, edited, reordered, deleted or validated, by any actor, whether or not index 0 is touched.
core.then: The repository's theme map MUST declare commons at theme index 0.
prefer: Add repository-specific themes at any other (non-zero) index, as long as each is a valid theme.
Ensure the end state has index 0 exactly commons — keep it there, or repair the map so it becomes commons if it is currently missing or wrong.
avoid: Replacing commons at index 0 with a repository-specific theme.
Removing the commons floor, leaving index 0 empty, or deleting the theme map file.
Moving commons to a different index or shifting another theme into index 0.
Adding other package-supplied entries to the map beyond the required index-0 commons.
core.why: Commons at index 0 is the mandatory, non-removable floor of every theme set; the rest of the map is owned by the repository and may be extended freely.
evidence: The theme map exists, parses, and its index-0 entry is commons.
The stack's static plan-artifact validator reports no finding for this rule.
verification: Fail if the theme map file is missing, or index 0 is missing, empty, or holds any value other than commons; other indexes may hold any valid theme. Evaluate the end-state map, not the diff.

Term 'resolved theme set' = the theme map declared in the theme-map plan artifact; values: floor = commons at index 0, removable = false. The repository-owned map is authoritative; the only package-supplied entry is index-0 commons.
Severity 4; disposition strict: the gate fails on every finding of this rule.
The check is a static validation of the theme-map plan artifact, run over the end state; the concrete validator identity and finding ids are realization details of each stack.

fires: The theme map is created for a repository.
A theme is added, renamed or removed at a non-zero index of the theme map (the whole map must still satisfy the invariant).
The index-0 entry (commons) is renamed, replaced or deleted.
The theme map is rewritten or reordered.
The theme map is deleted as a whole file.
Package-supplied entries are added to or removed from the map.
A static plan-artifact validation checks an existing repository's theme map, even if nobody changed it in the current task.
doesNotFire: Edits to product capabilities, DESIRED OUTCOMES, acceptances or other plan artifacts that only reference existing themes, when no validation of the theme map is being performed.

neutralityNotes: The rule is almost entirely neutral already: themes, commons-as-floor, product capabilities and DESIRED OUTCOMES are ATDD-method concepts, not stack mechanisms, so 'commons' is kept in the core. The only stack datum is the theme map's location (plan/_themes.yaml), supplied by the existing closed-vocabulary key layout.plan_item — the theme map is itself a plan artifact under the plan root, so no new key is needed (DESIRED OUTCOME in that key's example is illustrative, not a restriction). The Bun fact type 'path_glob' was mapped to the closed fact vocabulary as file_kind 'theme_map'. The concrete validator id (planner.static.validators.bun) and the alias/audit bookkeeping stay Bun-only; the strict-disposition shared node and severity 4 map to core:verification per the notProfileKeys rule. 'unless' is empty in bun.json and stays empty. Instantiating the core with layout.plan_item = plan/_themes.yaml plus the bunOnly validator reference reproduces bun.json's obligation exactly.
